title: Iterate on the core API (Docker Compose)
breadcrumb: Iterate on the core API (Docker Compose)

headings.text: Verify in rmlocal before trusting it
Switching between rmlocal and rmdev safely

blocks.html:
Once the legacy stack is up (see Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose)), this is the inner loop for changing the core rmapi: edit the source in the api/ submodule, let uvicorn reload it, exercise it, run integration tests against a clean database, then bring the change upstream. All commands assume the rmlocal / rmdev aliases from the setup page.

The edit / reload loop (rmdev)

The core source is the api/ git submodule, mounted into the rmapi container as /app. In rmdev the service runs under uvicorn --reload:

So the loop is:

  1. Edit Python under api/ (the rasenmaeher_api package).
  2. Save — uvicorn detects the change and reloads the app. No rebuild needed for pure Python edits.
  3. Hit the endpoint through the UI (https://localmaeher.dev.pvarki.fi:4439) or its Swagger UI, or via the relevant product callback path.
  4. Watch the container logs:
rmdev logs -f rmapi

Note: Reload covers source edits. Changing dependencies, the Dockerfile, or container-init.sh requires a rebuild: rmdev build rmapi then rmdev up -d rmapi. The dev entrypoint runs container-init.sh and poetry install before launching uvicorn, so dependency changes are picked up on container (re)start, not on file save.

Verify in rmlocal before trusting it

rmdev is convenient but introduces variability (reload, unminified assets, extra dev services). Before you consider a change done, confirm it in rmlocal, where assets are minified and baked in and the layout matches a real deployment:

rmdev down            # stop the dev env first (see rule below)
rmlocal build rmapi   # rebuild the baked image with your change
rmlocal up

Running integration tests

The integration tests require a clean database and have side effects (see Testing & CI conventions). Always reset volumes first:

rmlocal down -v       # wipe persistent volumes (deletes users/certs)
rmlocal build --pull
rmlocal up
# ... wait until healthy, then run the pytest integration suite

TODO: confirm the exact pytest invocation for the integration suite (host vs. inside the rmapi container) and document it here.

After any down -v, regenerate the first admin invite code before onboarding again:
rmlocal exec rmapi -it /bin/bash -c "source /.venv/bin/activate && rasenmaeher_api addcode"

Bringing the change upstream

Your edits live in the api/ submodule (pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api), a repo in its own right; the aggregate compose repo only records which commit of it to use. Per the compose README.rst "Git submodules", ship a core change in two steps:

  1. In the submodule (cd api/): branch, commit, push, and open a PR to pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api. Get it merged.
  2. In the compose repo: open a PR that updates the submodule pointer to the merged commit (check out the merged commit/tag inside api/, then git add api at the repo root, commit, and PR).

The detailed submodule-PR + compose-edit workflow (and the new-integration variant) is in Build an Integration > Register your integration (Docker Compose) — follow it there rather than repeating the steps. Remind collaborators to run git submodule update --init --recursive after pulling the pointer change.

Switching between rmlocal and rmdev safely

Two rules from the README.rst prevent most breakage:

  • Never keep both up at once. Running rmlocal and rmdev simultaneously causes network issues. Always down one before bringing up the other:

rmdev down
rmlocal up

• Use **down -v** to clear weird state. When switching environments or hitting inexplicable issues, reset the persistent volumes. Remember this destroys certificates and users, so you will re-run rasenmaeher_api addcode and re-onboard afterwards.
